dedupe_keys.name: agrifoodpy modular food system modelling framework with the agrifoodpy shocks resilience extension

description: AgriFoodPy is a Python framework for building models of a national food system, from food supply and consumption to land use and emissions, and its agrifoodpy-shocks extension adds crises and resilience interventions that perturb food supply. The producers are the AgriFoodPy developers of the FixOurFood project and the BAFR-UK project on food resilience in the United Kingdom. Coverage: the framework works with any country's FAOSTAT food balance sheets, and the companion data package holds UK data such as land classification and land cover. Models are chained as nodes in a pipeline over xarray data, for example loading food balance sheets, scaling consumption and projecting to 2050; the shocks extension registers crises such as a severe drought with a severity path and vulnerability by channel (biological, logistics, labour, market) and interventions that build resilience. The code is available on GitHub and PyPI under the free BSD 3-Clause licence, with documentation and examples. Caveats: it works at national, item-level aggregates, not on physical supply chain networks, the shocks extension is new and small, and results depend on assumed severity and vulnerability values. Simulation uses: stress tests of national food supply under harvest failures or trade disruption, comparing resilience interventions, and linking food availability to climate adaptation scenarios. Related records: FAOSTAT food balances (data-faostat) are its main input, and the global food shock trade model (model-global-food-shock-trade) covers cross-border propagation.
inputs: FAOSTAT food balance sheets by country, item and year
Population, land use and emissions data
Agricultural Land Classification and land cover maps for the UK (companion data package)
Crisis severity and vulnerability, intervention resilience by channel (biological, logistics, labour, market) for shock runs
